findings.summary: derivedGraphDocument in assets.ts was unreachable dead code AND actively harmful: it matched any module-export call whose arguments are static JSON, placed ahead of the module route that the node-particle family depends on, so zero-argument NPE factories matched first. Five stale executed-module bake entries containing NPE graph JSON prove scenes 277, 280, 284 and 301 were being routed through it. Deleted; all five scenes verified to regenerate byte-identically to main. The route it was written for never reached it, because the call is folded a level earlier at the const declaration.

The executed JSON pass ran in headless Chromium and recorded no adaptation, where every other browser bake in this repo has one. The repo already owns executed-module-graph, whose header argues that a graph is structure and cannot differ between two ECMAScript engines -- the browser-free route. Moved onto it, which removes the launch, the adaptation gap and the Chrome dependence in one go. Verified rather than asserted: the tree the Node run produces is byte-identical to the one Chromium produced. executed-module-assets.ts and bake-cache.ts are back to main untouched.

enableMorphTargetShadows reproduced the pin's arithmetic and dropped its refresh signal. The pin's proxy mesh also overrides worldMatrixVersion, bumped whenever the recomputed bounds change, so a morph WEIGHT change re-renders the shadow map with no transform moving. This port summed only transform and instance versions, so a scene animating weights without forceRefreshEveryFrame would have held a shadow map for a pose the mesh had left -- and scene 140, which sets that flag, is exactly the scene that cannot observe it. The weight version now joins the caster change signal for the generators that asked for the provider, and the docs no longer say the proxy has nothing left to do.

The pinned morph provider was anchored nowhere: the intrinsic reached the feature without asserting any pinned shape, so an upstream edit to the weighting would have compiled clean and fitted a different volume. Its registration and its expansion line are both pinned now, with the reason the body is transcribed rather than lowered stated where it is transcribed -- the pinned body is a method on an object literal, which lowerPinnedFunction does not reach.

The morph range cache claimed an invalidation it did not have: the comment said a geometry's deltas cannot change once loaded, but createMorphTargets clears and re-pushes them, keeping the same length, so a second call would have left the shadow fit using the first call's AABB. The cache is now dropped where the deltas are replaced, and the comment says the length test is a fill test rather than a freshness test.
The morph expansion skipped a target on weight == 0.0f where the pin's guard tests falsiness, so a NaN weight passed through here and poisoned the whole ortho fit rather than skipping one caster.

The folded-survivor mark stamped optionalFoundCpp on any surviving value kind when the dropped arm was nullish, but that field means presence and its consumers read it as truthiness. Those agree for a handle and part company for a value JavaScript calls falsy while holding it: `flag ? 0 : null` surviving as 0 would have folded `if (n)` to true. Narrowed to resources, and the dropped arm is now unwrapped so a parenthesized null is still seen.

probeStaticArrayLiteral lost its emission guard when the conditional fold was shared: several callers fall through on undefined, so a condition that emitted a temporary and then failed to fold would have leaked that emission into a lowering nobody kept. The guard is back, passed into the shared helper by the caller that needs it.

The conditional fold existed in three places -- a pre-existing loop in option-helpers and two new copies that had already diverged from each other over whether the condition is probed. One helper now, with the probe supplied by the caller that requires it.

The new regression test for the dangling-reference class was vacuous for the exact rule it protects: passesByReferenceKind has no optional arm, and picked_point is optional<tuple3>, so the rule was filtered out and deleting its flag left the test green. It now asks the type the aliasing decision actually runs on -- the narrowed inner -- and I proved it by removing the flag and watching it fail.

Four copies of the same generation-time child-process bridge (the sync asset read, the new JSON pass, the Canvas2D string and the fetched atlas) are one helper, so the spawn, the buffer size and the throw that prefers stderr over an errno have one home. Proven emission-neutral: the three scenes whose paths it touches regenerate byte-identically.

pinnedHypotCall was extracted with a docstring about keeping spellings from drifting, and three inline copies of it were left behind. All three routed through it; the generated tree is byte-identical, so this moved no emitted text.

pick_readback_row was introduced and four raw 256s left beside its uses, in a header whose own comment says a size mismatch truncates silently rather than failing. A named pick_depth_offset now covers them.

SDL and Dawn cleared the detail attachment with different words: SDL_FColor is float and 4294967295.0f is not representable, so it rounded to 4294967296.0 where Dawn's double was exact. Only a miss reads that texel and the decode returns before consuming it, which is precisely why nothing would have caught it. One home for the value, converted by each backend.
Two orphaned doc blocks, one per stream: assertFlagFalse's twin above the absence test, and the pin's ABSENT-test docstring stacked above staticallyAbsent instead of absenceTest.

The registry comment for scene 140 said all three of its contracts are reached, which is true, and left the reader to infer they are observed, which is not. forceRefreshEveryFrame is vacuous at a frozen pose -- the weights are set once, the camera does not move, so every frame after the first would be bit-identical with or without it. Said plainly now, alongside the morph note.

The fidelity A/B for the morph bounds contradicted its own numbers: it reported 0.048 to 0.047 and concluded the expansion does not change a pixel. It does -- and it is very slightly WORSE than not expanding. Rewritten to say that, and to say what would actually validate the provider, which is a scene that animates a weight and depends on the expansion. None is registered.

The purity argument for the executed JSON pass was false as stated: static arguments do not make a function pure, and the one function that meets the gate throws. The docs now say what the gate actually buys -- settled inputs, which is what makes the result a document rather than a computation over live state -- rather than claiming there is no runtime behaviour left.

The Math.hypot respelling moved 470 emitted call sites across six demos toward hypot_js, which fidelity.md records as an APPROXIMATION where std::hypot and V8 both use the overflow-safe scaled form. The change is defensible and was measured -- all nine affected scenes rebuilt and re-measured with every published number unchanged -- but the direction of the trade was not written down. It is now, in the adaptation that owns it.

An entire picking family shipped with no documentation: features.md still said the unsupported PickingInfo members refuse at the read site (eight of them no longer do), architecture.md still called the picking shaders two modules and the PAL attachments two, and the enableDetailedPicking divergence -- the pin's feature PROBE can answer no and leave picking coarse, this port answers yes and throws -- lived only in an emitted C++ comment. All four written up where this repo records such things, including the world-space detail position and why the barycentric solve is unaffected by it.

docs/features.md claimed the JSON pass reaches its evaluator through the same child process an uncached asset URL uses. It is a separate spawn of the same shape, which is what its own file says; corrected along with the route change.

A per-caster vector copy: the two weight lanes were selected with a ternary whose arms were a vector and an array, so the array arm had to be converted explicitly and the conditional's result became a prvalue that copied the storage lane whole, every caster of every refreshed generator, every frame. Pointers and a count instead.

populate_pick_ray transcribes the pin's createPickingRay line for line -- the NDC expressions, the near/far unprojection, the 1e-10 length guard -- in a file that goes to the trouble of lowering the module-private unprojectPoint from the pinned AST.
findings.blockedBy: The pinned function returns a record or null and the port writes into an out-parameter and returns void, so lowerPinnedFunction needs a returns shape it does not have today (an optional record built from a pinned object literal). That is a change to the lowering facility rather than to this scene, and it should land with a test over the facility rather than inside a scene wave whose proof burden is already two scenes on two backends.

findings.summary: ensure_morph_target_ranges is a third hand-typed copy of computeAabb's local arm, beside two pre-existing ones in mesh-builders and line-lowerer, in a repo that already lowers that pinned function from its AST in gizmo-lowerer.
findings.blockedBy: Collapsing them means one shared bbl::upstream::compute_aabb emitted with the geometry header and three call sites re-pointed, which moves emitted bytes in every mesh-builder and line scene. That wants its own differential sweep and a byte diff of the generated tree as its proof; folded into a wave whose diff is already two scenes' worth, that proof would be unreadable.

findings.summary: The morph expansion accumulates in float where the pin accumulates in double over a plain JS array, and docs/features.md calls it the pin's arithmetic.
findings.blockedBy: Widening the caster carrier's bounds to double changes the shadow fit's inputs for every shadow scene, not just the morph one, so it needs the whole shadow family re-measured. The divergence is also below the measurement floor at the one pose that reaches it, so there is no evidence to size the change against yet -- which is the same reason the provider itself is recorded as unvalidated.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the shadow-family entry

findings.summary: The morph-bounds helpers land in 15 trees that cannot reach them, 62,655 bytes, and the shadow header is not handed the feature list.
findings.blockedBy: The header emitter takes no features by design -- its own docstring says so, and the same limitation blocks the CSM gating already filed beside it -- and the PAL calls these helpers at runtime rather than at generation, so gating them needs a new compile define wired through CMake and both backends, not a generation-time conditional. That is feature-system work with its own build matrix, and gating emitted code has broken scenes reaching none of it three times in this project.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the shadow-family entry

findings.summary: The PCF SPOT factory still refuses forceRefreshEveryFrame while the machinery is shared and already built, and the refusal is now asserted in five places.
findings.blockedBy: Supporting it means emitting an option no registered scene reaches, which the repo's own convention argues against -- reach a capability where the pin's callers reach it. The asymmetry is stated deliberately in all five places rather than left as an oversight, and the anchor on the spot factory's own default means a pin that changed what it carries still fails. Closing it wants a scene, not a table entry.
findings.filedIn: src/compiler/intrinsics/shadow.ts and docs/features.md, stated as deliberate

findings.summary: Three copies of the detailed pick's CPU-array access materialize whole mesh arrays -- 197,916 bytes to read 48 -- because mesh_cpu_indices and friends return by value.
findings.blockedBy: mesh_cpu_indices is a straight return of the geometry's own vector and could be a reference, but the copies exist to preserve typed-array value semantics for SCENE code that reads them, and changing the helper's return type changes every scene-facing read of those three properties. Scene 113 picks once, so nothing in the gate can see it; the cost is on a hover path a real app would take, which is worth its own measured pass rather than a change made blind inside a scene wave.
